name: nom-longest-choice
instr:
Please add opt-in longest-match choice to nom in `/app`, so overlapping token parsers needn't put longest tokens first. Don't add new crates.

Expose `nom::branch::Choice<T, const LONGEST: bool = false, const UNIQUE: bool = false>`, with method `nom::branch::Choice::longest(self) -> Choice<T, true, false>` on `Choice<T, false, false>` and `nom::branch::Choice::unique(self) -> Choice<T, true, true>` on `Choice<T, true, false>`. Support tuples of 1 through 21 parsers, arrays and mutable slices. Ordinary `alt` remains first-success.

Add `nom::Parser::or_longest<G>(self, g: G) -> nom::OrLongest<Self, G>` where `Self: Sized`, `Input: nom::ChoiceInput`, and `G: Parser<Input, Output = Self::Output, Error = Self::Error>`. Expose `nom::OrLongest<F, G, const UNIQUE: bool = false>` implementing `Parser<I>` for matching children, with method `nom::OrLongest::unique(self) -> OrLongest<F, G, true>` on `OrLongest<F, G, false>`. Outputs needn't implement `Clone`.

Longest parsers require `I: nom::ChoiceInput`, not `Input`. Expose trait `nom::ChoiceInput: Clone` with method `nom::ChoiceInput::choice_len(&self) -> (usize, usize)`. Blanket-implement it for `I: Input` as `(input_len(), 0)`, and for bit cursors `(I, usize)` with `I: Input`: normalize remaining bits into `(whole_bytes, remaining_bits)` with the second component below 8, accepting offsets beyond 7. Custom implementations need no `Input`.

Call children once each, left to right, on original-input clones. Select the lexicographicall
